title: Who Pays for Friday Night?
narrativeQuestion: When an oil town in a bust hung its hopes on a team of teenagers in 1988, who ended up paying for Friday night, and what did the 2004 film change about the bill?

chapters.title: Kickoff
chapters.claim: Friday Night Lights is built on a real season: the 1988 Permian Panthers of Odessa, Texas, followed for a year by reporter H.G. Bissinger.

chapters.title: The Reporter
chapters.claim: Bissinger moved his family to Odessa in September 1988. His 1990 book sold about 2 million copies and became the 2004 film and the NBC series.

namedPeople.name: H.G. Bissinger
namedPeople.anchorNote: Photo slot listed in /storyhub/bts/friday-night/people/people.json for a teacher supplied photo. He also appears in the embedded 60 Minutes segment.

chapters.title: Boom and Bust
chapters.claim: Ratliff Stadium opened in 1982 near the top of the oil boom. By 1988 the average price of a barrel had fallen from $37.42 in 1980 to $14.87.

chapters.title: Mojo
chapters.claim: A $5.6 million stadium with 19,302 seats and four state titles behind them meant every Permian season was expected to end with a title run.

chapters.title: The Budget
chapters.claim: In 1988 the English department got $5,040 for materials while football spent $6,400 on game film, $6,750 on medical supplies and about $70,000 on chartered jets.

namedPeople.name: LaRue Moore
namedPeople.anchorNote: No openly licensed likeness. Her account is reported in Bissinger's text.

chapters.title: One Scrimmage
chapters.claim: Boobie Miles, recruited by major programs after 1,385 yards in 1987, hurt his knee in an August 1988 scrimmage in Lubbock and never got his career back.

namedPeople.name: James "Boobie" Miles
namedPeople.anchorNote: Photo slot listed in /storyhub/bts/friday-night/people/people.json. He also appears in the embedded 60 Minutes segment.

chapters.title: Heads or Tails
chapters.claim: After a 22 to 21 loss to Midland Lee, Permian's playoff life came down to a three coin flip at a truck stop just after midnight on November 5, 1988.

namedPeople.name: Gary Gaines
namedPeople.anchorNote: Photo slot listed in /storyhub/bts/friday-night/people/people.json. He appears in the embedded coin flip footage.

chapters.title: No Pass, No Play
chapters.claim: Texas made grades a condition of play in 1984. A disputed algebra grade let Dallas Carter keep playing, beat Permian 14 to 9 in Austin, and then lose its title in court on January 10, 1991.

namedPeople.name: Ross Perot
namedPeople.role: Chair of the 1984 Texas school reform committee

chapters.title: Hollywood or History
chapters.claim: The film keeps the big shape of the season but moves Boobie's injury, invents an easy win over Marshall and turns a rainy semifinal in Austin into a state final at the Astrodome.

chapters.title: The Town Fought Back
chapters.claim: Threats at an Odessa bookstore in 1990 made Bissinger cancel his signing there. He came back for the 25th anniversary in 2015.

chapters.title: The Tab
chapters.claim: Adding up the season shows the costs fell on people who never got a vote: a player's body, a classroom, a rival team, a school's title and the town's own story.
